verdict.rationale: OpenHands' own site describes an automation that detects failed workflows, inspects logs, identifies the likely cause, and opens a pull request with a proposed fix. Separately, automations are documented as able to run in response to webhook events from GitHub, which supports automatic triggering. This covers every element of the story, but only through short marketing-level claims. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on setting up and configuring the CI-failure automation, and independent or hands-on corroboration that the proposed fixes work.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can have failed CI workflows automatically diagnosed and fixed with a proposed pull request

citations.quote: Detect failed workflows, inspect logs, identify the likely cause, and open a pull request with a proposed fix.
